issues.failure_explanation: Abstract, introduction and conclusions present unconditional stability (for the Schrödinger scheme and, via Section 4, the wave scheme for all p) as proven without numerical verification. Theorem th:313 holds only under Assumption assu:34, and Theorem th:42 assumes an equivalent unique-solvability hypothesis. Unique solvability is proved only for p=1 or |mu|<pi/T and is otherwise supported only by numerical observation.

failure_location.quote: demonstrating that it preserves both mass and energy at the final time, and it is unconditionally stable

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State all stability claims (abstract, introduction, Section 4, conclusions) as conditional on Assumption assu:34, or supply a proof of discrete unique solvability for all p, h and mu.
issues.overall_effect: The headline guarantees are conditional on an unproven assumption, contrary to the advertised assumption-free, verification-free proof.
issues.title: Unconditional stability advertised as proven although it rests on an unproven uniqueness assumption
issues.why_classification: No proof changes, but the advertised guarantee type changes from unconditional to assumption-dependent. This is a material but limited weakening.

issues.failure_explanation: With w = e^{-t/T} d_t psi, the term i(d_t psi, w) = i * int |d_s psi|^2 e^{-s/T} is purely imaginary, so its real part is 0, not the positive integral. Moreover, since mu is any real number, the displayed sum with mu-weighted terms need not have a sign, so psi = 0 does not follow for mu < 0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take real and imaginary parts separately. The real part gives mu*(positive quantity) = 0, hence psi = 0 if mu is nonzero. For mu = 0 the imaginary part gives d_t psi = 0 and psi(0) = 0. Alternatively, use that the equation holds a.e. with zero initial datum.
issues.overall_effect: The uniqueness argument of Proposition prop:32 is invalid as written, though the statement is true.
issues.title: Invalid real-part computation in continuous uniqueness proof
issues.why_classification: A short local correction of the proof restores the full statement.

issues.failure_explanation: For hat functions, B[l,l] = (d_t phi_l, d_t phi_{l-1}) = -1/h and C[l,l] = 1/2. The diagonal of i B - mu C is therefore -(i/h + mu/2), not -(8i/h + mu/2).

failure_location.quote: is a lower triangular matrix with entries all equal to~$-\left(8\mi/h +\mu/2\right)$ on the diagonal

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the diagonal value by -(i/h + mu/2).
issues.overall_effect: The stated matrix entries are wrong. The invertibility conclusion for p=1 still holds because the diagonal has nonzero imaginary part.
issues.title: Incorrect diagonal entries claimed for the p=1 system matrix
issues.why_classification: A local correction that leaves the conclusion intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: meaning that if $\xi \in \mathbb{C}$ is a root of $q^{\K^p(\rho)}$, then $\xi^{-1}$ is also a root

issues.failure_explanation: q^B is palindromic and q^C anti-palindromic, so z^{2p} q(1/z) maps q^B + rho q^C to q^B - rho q^C, which is not a multiple of q^B + rho q^C. Hence xi being a root does not make 1/xi a root. For p=1 with the real form (eq:25), the roots are 1 and (1+rho/2)/(1-rho/2), of type (1,1,0) or (0,1,1), not (l, 2p-2l, l). With the correct symbol i q^B - rho q^C from eq:21, roots pair as xi and 1/conj(xi), which is not reciprocity.

failure_location.quote: it follows that $q^{\K^p(\rho)}$ is also a reciprocal polynomial for all $\rho \in \R$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use q^K = i q^B - rho q^C with real b_j, c_j. Show z^{2p} q^K(1/z) = -conj(q^K(conj z)), so roots are symmetric with respect to the unit circle. This gives type (l, 2p-2l, l).
issues.overall_effect: The type-(l,2p-2l,l) conclusion, needed to match the Amodio–Brugnano conditions, is not validly derived.
issues.title: Symbol of K is not reciprocal; reciprocity inferred from inconsistent symbol formula
issues.why_classification: A short replacement argument (self-inversive instead of reciprocal) restores the conclusion and all downstream results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For~$\rho>0$ and~$p \in \mathbb{N}$, the function $K_p(\theta,\rho)$ has exactly 2 simple zeros

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition prop:312 treats only rho>0, yet Theorem th:313 combines it to claim all rho in R. The case rho<0 is the dominant one, since mu = eigenvalues of (1/2)Delta + V are mostly negative. At rho=0, theta=0 is a double zero, so the Step-4 claim of exactly two simple zeros for all rho is false there.

failure_location.quote: Then, for all~$p \in \N$ and~$\rho \in \R$, the family of matrices~$\{\K_n^p(\rho)\}_n$ defined in~\eqref{eq:21} is weakly well-conditioned.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the symmetry K_p(-theta,-rho) = K_p(theta,rho) (B_p even, C_p odd) to treat rho<0. Treat rho=0 separately: count the double unimodular zero, or use weak well-conditioning of B.
issues.overall_effect: Weak well-conditioning for rho <= 0, the relevant regime for most spectral modes, is not covered by the cited propositions.
issues.title: Main theorem claimed for all real rho but zero count proved only for rho>0
issues.why_classification: A routine symmetry argument plus a degenerate-case remark restores the full statement.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we show that, for all $p \in \N$ and $\mu \in \R$, the condition number of~$\K_h^p(\mu)$, as a function of~$h$, does not grow exponentially

issues.failure_explanation: Theorems th:38/th:39 give, for each fixed symbol (fixed rho), a power growth in n with rho-dependent constants. For fixed mu, refining h changes rho = mu h toward 0, where the two unimodular roots coalesce. For the fully discrete scheme, rho ranges over all mu_{h_x} h_t. No bound uniform in rho is shown, so the fixed-rho result does not establish the stated h-dependence for fixed mu or the absence of a CFL restriction.

failure_location.quote: In other words, the variational formulation in \eqref{eq:10} is

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove conditioning bounds polynomial in n uniformly in rho (including rho -> 0 and |rho| large). Otherwise, restrict the claim to families with fixed rho = mu h.
issues.overall_effect: The translation of the matrix result into unconditional stability of eq:10, eq:7 and eq:30 is unsupported.
issues.title: Fixed-rho conditioning does not yield stability for fixed mu as h->0 or uniformly over the spectrum
issues.why_classification: Restoring the advertised claim needs a contained but nontrivial uniform estimate. Otherwise the stability notion must be weakened.

issues.failure_explanation: Factoring eq:35 as (iB⊗I)(I⊗M + QRQ^H⊗A) gives (R⊗A + I⊗M) Z = (Q^H⊗I)(iB⊗I)^{-1} F with Psi = (Q⊗I) Z. Step 4 uses R^{-1}⊗M instead of I⊗M, which is not equivalent since R ≠ I. Step 2 drops the factor i, and the sign in step 5 (-1 rather than -i) does not compensate. The output is therefore not the solution of eq:35.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Solve (iB⊗I)Y = F, update Y by (Q^H⊗I), solve (R⊗A + I⊗M)Z = Y (or its R^{-1}-premultiplied equivalent), and set Psi = (Q⊗I)Z.
issues.overall_effect: The described solver does not compute the discrete solution as written.
issues.title: Bartels–Stewart steps do not solve the stated linear system
issues.why_classification: A routine re-derivation of standard Bartels–Stewart steps fixes the algorithm with no loss of efficiency or scope.
